description_en: Constructed during the reign of King Pārthivendra Malla in 1684–85 CE (NS805), this temple ranks among the few monuments in Kathmandu that remained structurally intact following the recent devastating earthquakes.The temple stands prominently along the main street of Cikamugaḥ Ṭola, an old quarter wheresataḥs,phalcās(public rest platforms), and numerous shrines line both sides of the road. Since the medieval period, this street—where the chariotof Kumārī is also assembled—has served as one of the principal thoroughfares of the city and a residential area for noble and elite families. Many of the religious monuments along this street were constructed by such local aristocratic lineages during the late medieval period. Among these is the present temple dedicated to Nārāyaṇa.The three-tiered temple faces west toward the street. It is notable for being apagoda-style structure raised entirely on brick walls without the use of supporting wooden pillars on the ground level—a rare architectural form. Only a few comparable examples exist, such as the temples of Gokarṇa (GKN0010), Jalavināyaka (CHO0100), and Indreśvara in Panauti. Though modest in scale, this temple is considered a rare and refined example of this architectural category.The entrance door leading to thegarbhagṛha(sanctum) is exquisitely carved, exhibiting the intricate workmanship characteristic of the late medieval period. Thetoraṇaabove the door has been lost, yet the craftsmanship of the carved wooden frame—with its detailed floral motifs and delicate carving—recalls the artistic standards of the era. The cornices (karnisa) and struts (tuṇḍāla) are similarly ornamented with elaborate woodwork. Only the corner brackets (kuṃsala) and a few upper-tier struts have survived, while 32 historic struts on the first and second roof levels were replaced with plain wooden brackets to support the roof. All three roofs are covered with traditionaljhiṅgaṭītiles and crowned with a gilt brassgajūra(pinnacle).Inside thegarbhagṛharesides the principal icon—a stone image of Nārāyaṇa. The sculpture is remarkable for its detailed pedestal (pādapīṭha) and uniqueprabhā(aureole) carved not as a halo but as a stylizedkadambatree, as explicitly mentioned in the inscription found below the image. At the center of the pedestal, Garuḍa is depicted, flanked by small donor figures shown innamaskāraposture. According to oral testimony (Śreṣṭha, male, age 65), the original grand image of Viṣṇu, which matched the scale and style of the pedestal andprabhā, was stolen during the 1960s CE (2020s VS). The current image, recovered from a police storehouse, was subsequently installed as a replacement. Although the proportions differ from the original, the extant sculpture also dates from the late medieval period. Flanking the main statue are subsidiary icons of Candra and Sūrya, while smaller images of Bhīmasena, Garuḍa, and another Viṣṇu—brought from other locations—are also housed within the sanctum.An inscription carved on the front face of the pedestal records the installation of the Viṣṇu statue in 1684–85 CE (NS 805), during the reign of Pārthivendra Malla. It mentions a certain Nayana Bhāro of Ponde Ṭola (a sub-quarter within Cikaṃmugaḥ) as the artisan who crafted the statue and itskadambavṛkṣa-prabhā. The lower lines of the inscription are now completely eroded, but it is evident that the same Nayana Bhāro was responsible for constructing the three-tiered shrine itself. The Bhāros of Cikaṃmugaḥ—associated with the Joshi, Māthema, and Śreṣṭha lineages—were prominentbhāradāras(court officials) during the Malla period, and the builder likely belonged to one of these influential families. Pruscha (1975, p. 77), however, mistakenly attributed the temple’s construction to the reign of King Bhūpatindra Malla.One of the remarkable features of this monument is its survival in an unaltered, original form. While hundreds of temples across the valley were destroyed or heavily restored following the 2015 CE (VS 2072) earthquake—many unnecessarily, with traditionaljhiṅgaṭīroofs replaced by copper sheets—this temple has remained largely untouched, preserving its authentic medieval character.The temple’s system ofnitya(daily) andvārsika(annual) rituals has long fallen into disuse. Elderly residents report that in their lifetime, no active worship has been conducted here under theguthi(endowment) system once associated with the shrine.
description_ne: पार्थिवेन्द्र मल्लको शासनकाल अर्थात् नेसं ८०५ (सन् १६८४-८५) मा बनेको यो मन्दिर पछिल्लो भूकम्पमा क्षति नभएका काठमाडौंका सीमित मन्दिरमध्येमा पर्दछ ।चिकंमुगः टोलमा मुख्य सडक किनारामा सतः, फल्चा र अनेक मन्दिरहरू बनेका छन् । कुमारीको रथ कुडाइने चिकंमुगःको यो सडक मध्यकालदेखि मुख्य सडकका रूपमा रही आएको छ र यस सडक किनार कुलीन खलकहरूको निवासस्थल रही आएको छ । ती खलकबाट यहाँ यी सम्पदाहरू उत्तरमध्यकालमा बनेका थिए । यस सडक किनारमा भएका सम्पदामध्ये यो नारायणको मन्दिर पनि एक हो । सडकतिरै फर्किएको अर्थात् पश्चिमाभिमुख यो मन्दिर तीनतले छ । भूमि तलामा थामा नभई इँटको गारो उठाइएका तीन तले पेगोडा मन्दिर निकै कम संख्यामा पाइन्छन् । गोकर्ण मन्दिर (GKN0010), जलविनाय मन्दिर (CHO0100) र पनौतीको इन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिर यो शैलीका सीमित उदाहरणमा पर्दछन् । आकारमा सानो भए तापनि यसै कोटीको स्वरूपमा बनेको यस मन्दिरलाई पनि एक दुर्लभ उदाहरण मान्न सकिन्छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृह प्रवेश गर्ने ढोका कलात्मक छ । ढोकामाथिको तोरण हराई सकेको छ । मध्यकालीन काँठको ढोकामा पाइने कलात्मक कालिगढी यहाँको ढोकामा पनि देख्न सकिन्छ । ढोकाका अलावा कार्निस एवं टुँडाल पनि समान स्तरका बुट्टादेर काष्ठकलाबाट सजिएको छ । कुनाका कुँसल र माथिल्लो तलाका टुँडालमात्र यहाँ बच्न सम्भव भएको छ । बाँकी प्रारम्भिक टुँडालहरू लोप भैसकेका छन् र तिनका ठाउँमा सादा काँठ हाली छाना थमाइएको छ । तीनै तलामा झिंगटीको प्रयोग भएको मन्दिरमा धातुको गजूर चढाइएको छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा मुख्य मूर्तिका रूपमा नारायणको शिलामूर्ति छ । यहाँ मूर्तिको पाद र मूर्ति पछाडिको प्रभा विशेष छ । मूर्तिको पादको केन्द्रमा गरुड कुँदिएको छ र उनको दायाँ-बायाँ दाता परिवारको नमस्करण मुद्रामा कुँदिएका शालिक छन् । मूर्ति पछाडि प्रभामण्डल नभई वृक्षको प्रभा कुँदिएको छ । यहाँ भएको अभिलेखमा यस प्रभालाई कदमवृक्षको प्रभा भनिएको छ । यहाँ पादपीठ र प्रभा जस्तै विशेष आकर्षण भएको विष्णुको भव्य मूर्ति हुने गर्दथ्यो । विसं २०२० को दशकमा सो मूर्ति चोरी भए पश्चात् प्रहरी चौकीको भण्डारमा भएको अर्कै विष्णुमूर्ति ल्याई प्रतिस्थापन गरिएको थियो (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 65) । यसर्थ पाद र प्रभावको आकारप्रकार र भव्यतासँग वर्तमानमा भएको मूर्ति मेल खादैन । तथापि, वर्तमानमा भएको मूर्ति पनि उत्तरमध्यकालीन नै हो । मुख्य मूर्तिका साथमा दायाँ-बायाँ चन्द्र र सूर्यका मूर्ति राखिएका छन् । अन्त कतैबाट ल्याई भीमसेन, गरुड र अर्को एक सानो विष्णुमूर्ति पनि यहाँको गर्भगृहमा राखिएको छ ।गर्भगृहमा भएको पादपीठको अग्रभागमा अभिलेख कुँदिएको छ । सो अभिलेख अनुसार यहाँ नेसं ८०५ (सन् १६८४-८५) अर्थात् पार्थिवेन्द्र मल्लको शासनकालमा यो विष्णुमूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको प्रसंग छ । पोन्दे टोल (मन्दिर अवस्थित चिकंमुगः अन्तर्गतको उप-टोल) का नयन भारोले कदमवृक्षको प्रभा हाली मूर्ति बनाए भन्ने सम्मको वाक्यांश अभिलेखमा पढ्न सकिन्छ । अभिलेखका तल्लो पंक्ति पूर्णतः खिई सकेका छन् । उनैले मूर्तिसँगै यो तीनतले मन्दिर बनाएको देखिन्छ । चिकंमुगःमा जोशी, माथेमा र श्रेष्ठ जस्ता भारदार (भारो) खलकहरू बस्दै आएका छन् । निर्माता नयन भारो यी तीममध्ये कुनै खलकका पूर्वज देखिन्छन् । Pruscha (1975, p. 77) ले राजा पार्थिवेन्द्रलाई गल्तीवस भूपतिन्द्र भनी उनको पालामा मन्दिर बनेको भनेका छन् ।यो मन्दिरको एक विशेषता भनेको मौलिक स्वरूपमै अस्तित्वमा रहन सक्नु हो । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को महाभुकम्प पश्चात् सयौं मन्दिर भत्की-बिग्री पुनर्निर्माण गरिए । कतिपय मन्दिरहरू अनावश्य रूपमै पुनर्निर्माण गरिए । भूकम्प पछि थुप्रै मन्दिरका छानामा झिंगटी हटाई तामाको पाता विछ्याउने कार्य भए । तर यो मन्दिर पुरानै स्वरूपमा हालसम्म उभिन सकेको छ ।यस मन्दिरको नित्य एवं वार्षिक पूजा प्रणाली लोप भैसकेको छ । स्थानीय वृद्धवृद्धा यस मन्दिर सम्बद्ध गुठी एवं गुठी प्रणालीबाट यहाँ कुनै पूजा हुने गरेको आफ्नो जीवनकालमा नदेखेको बताउँछन् ।

historical_events.event_description: Nayana Bhāro of Cikaṃmugaḥ, Ponde Ṭola, established a grand stone image of Nārāyaṇa adorned with akadambavṛkṣa-prabhāand constructed the temple to enshrine it.
Harinandan Joshi erected a pillar supporting a Garuda statue in front of the temple. Today, only the pillar remains, as the Garuḍa statue was likely stolen.

Rudrasiṃha Bhāro donated his residential house and adjoining land for religious purposes dedicating to his ancestralāgama-devatā(family tutelary deity). Although the exact date of the inscription is unclear, the language and script suggest that it belongs to the late medieval period.

Verse 1:In the year 1776 CE (ŚS 1698), on an auspicious day in the month of Kārtika, under theUttarabhādrapadāconstellation and the holy occasion ofHaribodhinī Ekādaśī, when the moon was in Mīnarāśi, and both Jupiter (Guru) and Venus (Śukra) were in favorable positions—at that propitious moment, the minister Śrīkīrtisiṃha commenced the construction of this grand Jaya Maṇḍira.Verse 2:The king, sovereign of the Gaurśācala realm, had a contented land and a joyous populace. His minister, the learned and valiant Kīrtisiṃha, was served by his attendant, Sarūpasiṃha. In thisJayamaṇḍira, Lord Śaṅkara Mahādeva himself dwells in full glory; may the blessings of Lambodara Gaṇeśa ever abide here.Verse 3:May horses and elephants playfully roam here; may dancers perform in every direction; may hymns, devotional songs, andpurāṇarecitations resound daily; may children and subjects remain ever joyful; may kinsmen and women vie in beauty; and may all reside fearlessly in thisJayamaṇḍira, thereby increasing its glory (kīrti).

This inscription does not originally belong to the temple but has been brought from elsewhere. The upper portion of the stone stele is engraved with avajra(thunderbolt) and the text records that a family of Dhījavirasiṃha from Kāntipura (Kathmandu) constructed avajradhātu caitya.
